newsitem.title: CANADA: GM, Canada union agree on outsourcing.
newsitem.headline: GM, Canada union agree on outsourcing.

text.p: General Motors Corp. and the Canadian Auto Workers union said on Monday they resolved the thorny issue of outsourcing and were near a deal to end a two-week old strike.
CAW President Buzz Hargrove, asked if a tentative contract agreement was likely in time to meet a self-imposed noon EDT deadline on Monday for a settlement, responded:
"I'd say that was a fair assessment. We have resolved the issue of outsourcing," Hargrove told Reuters during a break in contract talks that lasted all weekend.
Hargrove said the 26,000 striking workers, who hit the picket lines on Oct. 2, could start returning to work as soon as Wednesday afternoon if a tentative deal were reached Monday.
"Everyone can start returning to work by late Wednesday," he said.

GM Canada spokesman Stew Low said there was enough of an agreement on outsourcing for him to be confident of a deal, which meets the labour agreement pattern the union set at Chrysler Corp. earlier this year.
"I think there is enough common ground for the CAW to say they have met the pattern and hopefully our needs as well," Low said.
Both sides cautioned that there were still sticking points that could derail the talks, such as overtime rules at the Oshawa, Ontario complex of the world's largest carmaker.
"The latest read I had was there was still a lot of work there at the Oshawa local," Low said.
But local union officials from Oshawa told Reuters that the "floodgates had opened" on the outsourcing issue and a deal there was likely.
